facts.value: Two Treasury Management Monitoring reports on the Council 25 November 2025 pack: Q1 (1 April to 30 June 2025, doc 7236) and H1/mid-year (1 April to 30 September 2025, doc 7237). H1 is the paper explicitly recommended to Council. Both 9-page PDFs from Director of Corporate Resources/Deputy CEO.

source.title: Treasury Management Monitoring Report 1 April 2025 to 30 September 2025 — Council, 25 November 2025, agenda paper 7237 (H1); background paper 7236 (Q1) also on the pack

facts.note: 7237 (H1) went first to Governance & Standards Committee on 19 November 2025 with a recommendation to Council 25 November; 7236 (Q1) had earlier gone to Governance & Standards on 24 September 2025 and sits on the Council pack as background. Treasury advisor MUFG (para 4.4 of both). 2025/26 Treasury Management Strategy approved by Council 4 March 2025. All treasury figures below cited to page numbers, marked (7236) or (7237).

facts.value: £70.826m total external borrowing at 30 September 2025 — £50.673m PWLB (unchanged since 30 June), £20.000m other Local Authorities (+£10m in Q2), £0.153m short-term Racecourse Trust
facts.note: Walk across the year: 31.3.25 £56,326k → 30.6.25 £60,826k (+£4.5m) → 30.9.25 £70,826k (+£10m). All net new borrowing in 2025/26 has been from other local authorities; PWLB book static at £50.673m across both quarters. Short-term Racecourse Trust £153k unchanged throughout.

facts.value: NOT DISCLOSED in either monitoring paper — referenced in both papers' para 4.1 as set out in the 2025/26 Treasury Management Strategy approved 4 March 2025, but no numeric value printed
facts.note: The 2025/26 Approved Operational Boundary Borrowing component is £194,715k and Authorised Limit £202,715k (7237 Table 5, p.6). By convention CFR sits at or below Operational Boundary — so ≤ ~£195m — but no specific CFR figure is stated. Would sit in the 4 March 2025 Strategy paper (not on this pack). Absence noted.

facts.value: £5.802m actual at 30 September 2025; £5.775m projected 2025/26 outturn; Operational Boundary £5.669m, Authorised Limit £7.669m
facts.note: OLTL at 30 September 2025 is £5.802m — sits ABOVE the £5.669m Operational Boundary but BELOW the £7.669m Authorised Limit. Same figure at 30 June 2025 (7236 Table 5). Projected outturn £5.775m assumes some run-off during H2. No detail on what the OLTL comprises (IFRS 16 leases, PFI, or other) — paper does not elaborate.

facts.value: NOT PERFORMABLE from these papers. CFR not printed, so internal borrowing cannot be computed.
facts.note: Arithmetic: internal borrowing = CFR − external borrowing (£70,826k at 30.9.25) − OLTL (£5,802k at 30.9.25) = CFR − £76,628k. CFR is not disclosed in either paper. Under-borrowing quantum cannot be quoted or verified. Not raised with the council — absence of CFR is a paper-scope observation, not something to correct.

facts.value: £26,153k of the £70,826k total external borrowing matures inside 12 months at 30 September 2025 — 37% of the book
facts.note: Full maturity profile at 30.9.25: <1yr £26,153k (37%), 1-2yr £0, 2-5yr £12,173k (17%), 5-10yr £2,000k (3%), >10yr £30,500k (43%). Barbell shape — no holdings in the 1-2yr bucket, sparse 2-10yr, heavy at both ends. <1yr bucket rose from £9,653k at 31.3.25 to £16,153k at 30.6.25 to £26,153k at 30.9.25, largely tracking the £10m of new LA borrowing added in Q2 plus one existing loan rolling into <1yr through the year.

facts.value: At 30 September 2025: £30.0m at less than 3% (7 loans), £40.826m between 3% and 5% (11 loans). Nothing above 5%.

source.title: 7237 Table 2, Long Term Borrowing by Interest Rate, p.3

facts.note: £30m cheap fixed core below 3% is stable across the year (unchanged 31.3.25 to 30.9.25). The 3-5% bucket picked up £10.826m in Q2 — matching the £10m LA borrowing plus £0.826m of miscellany. Table 1 and Table 2 both total 18/£70,826k at 30.9.25 but at earlier dates the loan-count columns diverge (Table 1: 17, Table 2: 15 at 30 June); £-figures reconcile at both tables so this is a counting-basis quirk, not a value discrepancy. Not raised.

facts.value: £20m of new loans taken in April–September 2025 (all from other Local Authorities); anticipated £50m for full year 2025/26, revised up from £40m in the Q1 report
facts.note: MID-YEAR REVISION: the anticipated 2025/26 borrowing figure moved from £40m in the Q1 report (para 4.1 of 7236) to £50m in the H1 report (para 4.1 of 7237) — a 25% upgrade disclosed inside two months with no narrative for the change. Table 5 projected outturn Borrowing rose consistently from £86,826k to £96,826k. £30m of further draws implied in H2 against the £50m plan (£50m plan less £20m drawn). PWLB book untouched all year — every pound of the £20m has been inter-LA.

facts.value: £25.500m invested at 30 September 2025 (£10m DMO 39%, £5.5m Svenska Handelsbanken instant access 22%, £10m across four LA counterparties). +£8m from 30 June.
facts.note: LA counterparties at 30.9.25: Aberdeen City £2m, Blackpool £4m, Derbyshire CC £2m, Eastleigh BC £2m. Walk across year: 30.9.24 £39m → 31.3.25 £17m → 30.6.25 £17.5m → 30.9.25 £25.5m. Investment book has grown £8.5m across Q1+Q2 broadly matching the £20m of new LA borrowing (net of £11.5m ordinary spend). Lloyds current account cap £3m per Strategy (para 5.8). Banking contract extended to March 2027 (para 5.7).

facts.value: Average yield 4.53% year to date at 30 September 2025 — beats Base Rate (4.21%) by 32bp, Money Market (4.19%) by 34bp, Lloyds (4.11%) by 42bp. Projected outturn £200k above the £535k budget.
facts.note: Yield walk across recent periods: 2023/24 4.81%, 2024/25 5.14%, Q1 2025/26 4.71%, H1 2025/26 4.53%. Bank Rate fell 5.25% to 4.00% July 2024 to August 2025 (para 6.3). Projected outperformance vs budget was £135k at Q1 report, stepped up to £200k at H1 — implies £735k projected outturn against £535k budget (37% over).

facts.value: MRP policy not discussed in either monitoring paper beyond a Section 11(a) legal reference to 'MRP Guidance'. Detail would sit in the 4 March 2025 Strategy paper (not on this pack).
facts.note: Absence recorded, not raised — a monitoring report is not expected to restate MRP policy in full.

facts.value: Not mentioned in either monitoring paper. No chart, no numbers, no reference to the four Code components.
facts.note: Absence recorded. Would normally live in a Strategy paper, not a monitoring report. Worth mentioning softly in the email as a standing observation — CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates put the LB further in front of every S151.

facts.value: 2025/26 Approved Operational Boundary £200.384m total (Borrowing £194.715m + OLTL £5.669m). Actual at 30 September 2025: £76.628m (38% of Operational Boundary).
facts.note: Substantial headroom throughout — even the projected outturn at year-end £102.601m still leaves £97.783m of unused Operational Boundary. Not the binding constraint on borrowing decisions.

facts.value: 2025/26 Approved Authorised Limit £210.384m total (Borrowing £202.715m + OLTL £7.669m). Actual at 30 September 2025 sits at 36% of Authorised Limit.
facts.note: Statutory ceiling under s.3(1) Local Government Act 2003. £10m above Operational Boundary. No breach; para 7.3 verbatim: 'During the financial year to date the Council has, at all times operated within the treasury limits and prudential indicators as set out in the Council's Treasury Management Strategy.'

facts.value: MUFG newsflash 11 August 2025 (per 7237 para 6.5): base rate at 4.00%, no further reduction expected at November 2025 MPC. Current expectation: base rate reaches 3.75% by March 2026.
facts.note: Q1 report had said 4.25% by May 2025 (achieved) then holding, with the 3.75% March 2026 end-year still in view. The 3.75% March 2026 forecast is unchanged between the Q1 and H1 reports despite two intervening base rate cuts. Advisor MUFG throughout.

signals.headline: £26.153m — 37% of the £70.826m external borrowing book — matures inside 12 months at 30 September 2025, against nothing in the 1-2yr bucket and £12.173m in 2-5yr
signals.why_it_matters: Barbell rather than laddered. Combined with the anticipated £30m of new drawings still to arrange in H2 2025/26, the near-term rate call dominates the treasury decisions of the next 12-24 months, against MUFG's forecast of base rate reaching 3.75% by March 2026.

signals.headline: Anticipated 2025/26 borrowing revised up from £40m to £50m between the Q1 and H1 monitoring reports — a 25% upgrade disclosed inside two months without narrative for the change
signals.why_it_matters: Consistent with the Table 5 projected outturn Borrowing rising £86,826k → £96,826k across the two reports. £20m drawn to date, all inter-LA; leaves £30m of further arrangements against the £50m anticipated. No PWLB drawn all year despite the falling base-rate environment.

signals.headline: External borrowing has grown £14.5m across the first half of 2025/26 (£56.326m to £70.826m), entirely funded from the inter-authority market — PWLB book static at £50.673m all year
signals.why_it_matters: Deliberate choice to lean on the LA market for new borrowing while keeping PWLB dry. Consistent with MUFG's forecast that base rate falls, which favours shorter-dated LA borrowing over locking in longer PWLB now.

summary.text:
Two treasury monitoring reports on the Mansfield Council pack of 25 November 2025 — the Q1 report (doc 7236, first heard 24 September 2025) and the H1/mid-year report (doc 7237, first heard 19 November 2025 and explicitly recommended to Council). Both 9-page PDFs from the Director of Corporate Resources/Deputy CEO; treasury advisor is MUFG. Every treasury figure is machine-cited to page and paper.

Balance-sheet identity NOT PERFORMABLE from these papers. Both reports reference the CFR (para 4.1 of each) as sitting in the 4 March 2025 Treasury Management Strategy but neither monitoring paper prints a CFR value. Internal borrowing = CFR − £70,826k external − £5,802k OLTL = CFR − £76,628k at 30 September 2025 — cannot be computed. Under-borrowing quantum not stated. Absence recorded, not raised: a monitoring paper referring back to Strategy for CFR is normal practice.

Loan-book reconciliation FAILED — coverage gap on our side. Paper reports £50.673m PWLB at 30 September 2025, unchanged from 30 June (para 4.6). Our bc-loans file holds 14 total loans / £54,673,000 principal (13 live at 14 August 2026 / £52,673,000) — £2m higher than the paper's PWLB balance. bc-loans 'start' field returns no loans outstanding at 2025-09-30 — matches the EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md warning that start dates are unreliable. Per pipeline rule the loan-book claim is left out of the email entirely, no figure quoted from either side.

Distinctive shape is on the borrowing profile. External borrowing has grown £14.5m across H1 2025/26 (£56.326m to £70.826m) and every pound of the £20m of new drawings has come from the inter-authority market — PWLB static at £50.673m across both quarters. Anticipated 2025/26 borrowing revised UP from £40m (Q1 report) to £50m (H1 report) — a 25% upgrade inside two months, with the projected outturn Borrowing on Table 5 stepping consistently £86,826k → £96,826k. £30m of further draws implied in H2 against the £50m plan.

Barbell maturity profile. Table 1 at 30 September shows £26,153k (37% of £70,826k) maturing inside 12 months, £0 in the 1-2yr bucket, £12,173k in 2-5yr, £2,000k in 5-10yr and £30,500k (43%) beyond 10 years. The £30m fixed core below 3% is unchanged across the year; the 3-5% bucket picked up the £10m of new LA money in Q2.

Investment performance strong. Average yield 4.53% year to date, beating Base Rate by 32bp, Money Market by 34bp and Lloyds by 42bp (Table 4). Projected outperformance vs the £535k budget rose from £135k (Q1) to £200k (H1) — 37% over budget projected for the full year. Investment book grew £8m in Q2 (£17.5m to £25.5m) as the new LA borrowing built cash balances.

Papers are bare compared with most in the library. No CFR, no liability benchmark, no MRP policy discussion, no financing costs ratio, no LOBOs, no HRA/GF split, no IFRS 16 note. Just borrowing, investments and prudential limits vs actual/outturn. The underlying treasury detail sits in the 4 March 2025 Strategy paper which is not on this Council pack — so a thin monitoring report is not necessarily a thin treasury operation. Email is drafted off the maturity/LA-choice hooks; the absent items are recorded here.

No officer address published on the paper. Report author block on p.9 of both papers names Dave Wayne, Financial Advisor (dwayne@mansfield.gov.uk, 01623 463074) — an author, not the S151. The Section 151 Officer is referenced by title in section 12(b) of both papers but the name is not printed on either paper. Report is from the Director of Corporate Resources/Deputy CEO but no name on the front sheet. Contact scan required before send. Do NOT guess the S151's title.

[INTERNAL ONLY] Table 1 (maturity) and Table 2 (interest rate) use slightly different counting bases across the year — at 30.9.25 both reconcile to 18 loans / £70,826k, but at 30.6.25 Table 1 shows 17 loans and Table 2 shows 15. The £-totals reconcile at both tables so this is a counting-basis quirk (LA and Trust rows treated differently), not a value discrepancy. Not raised.

officer.body:
Dear [OFFICER],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on the H1 Treasury Management Monitoring report that went to Council on 25 November, alongside the Q1 report on the same pack. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Both reports are clean and easy to read across, and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The first thing that jumped out is on where the new borrowing has come from. Your PWLB book at £50.673m hasn't moved a pound in either quarter — paragraph 4.6 shows the same figure at 30 June and 30 September. Every pound of the £20m taken in the first half has come from other local authorities. That's a choice worth naming: many councils in the same window went to PWLB for short tenors and paid the certainty rate for the privilege. Your inter-LA route usually prices tighter for one-year money and does not need Debt Management Account paperwork — the daily PWLB fixings and the monthly inter-LA volumes both sit on the platform if it helps see where the sector has been clearing.

The other shape is the maturity profile in Table 1. £26.153m — 37% of the £70.826m total — sits in the under-one-year bucket at 30 September, against nothing at all in the one-to-two-year bucket, £12.173m in two-to-five and £30.5m beyond ten. That's a barbell, not a laddered book. Combined with the anticipated £50m of borrowing for the full year in paragraph 4.1 (raised from £40m in the Q1 report), and with £20m already drawn, roughly £30m of new borrowing plus the £26m of rolls to organise in the coming twelve months. All against the base-rate walk paragraph 6.6 expects to reach 3.75% by March.

On investments, you're doing well against benchmarks. Table 4 shows your 4.53% average for the year to date against 4.21% Base Rate, 4.19% Money Market and 4.11% Lloyds — a 32 to 42 basis point lift depending which comparator. Paragraph 6.4 projects £200,000 above the original £535,000 budget, up from £135,000 called at Q1. The £8m of investment book growth in Q2 sits alongside the LA borrowing on the other side of the balance sheet.
